The African Democratic Congress (ADC) said it has presented 17 grounds to set aside Justice Peter O. Lifu’s judgment which sacked the David Mark-led executive of the party on 5 November 2026 at the Court of Appeal.
The party said it also challenged the earlier ruling that allowed Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe to amend his suit despite the ADC’s unresolved objection to the trial court’s jurisdiction. The ADC said it will not accept a judgment that it contends was built on a case the court had no authority to hear.
In a statement issued by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, the party said its Notice of Appeal challenges the trial court’s jurisdiction to decide what the ADC maintains is an internal party leadership dispute. It also questions the court’s treatment of an earlier Federal High Court judgment on the leadership transition, delivered on 2 July 2026, which the party says had not been set aside.
“The 17 grounds challenge the foundation, findings and orders of Justice Lifu’s judgment. The ADC has asked the Court of Appeal to examine whether the trial court had jurisdiction, whether the claimant had standing, whether disputed evidence was properly assessed, and whether the sweeping orders made against the party can stand in law,” Shaibu said.
In its separate appellant’s brief challenging the ruling of 24 July 2026, the ADC argues that the court granted Gombe leave to amend his originating summons while deferring its decision on the party’s preliminary objection to jurisdiction. The brief contends that the motion seeking amendment had altered the description of parties and the capacity in which a defendant was sued without prior leave of court.
That brief was settled by Chief J. S. Okutepa, SAN, lead counsel for the ADC in the appeal against the amendment ruling. It asks the Court of Appeal to set aside the order granting amendment and consider the outstanding jurisdictional objection.
The ADC has also asked the Court of Appeal for an injunction to prevent the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from changing the party’s leadership records or interfering with the names and nomination particulars of its presidential and governorship candidates while the appeal is heard.
The party argued that Justice Lifu’s judgment rests on an amended court process that was already under appeal, yet the trial court proceeded to judgment before that appeal was resolved. If INEC acts on the judgment now, the ADC says, the resulting changes could be difficult to undo and could render a successful appeal meaningless. The party is asking the appellate court to preserve the position that existed before the 5 November judgment.
“These are serious questions before the Court of Appeal. INEC must not make changes that could preempt the court’s decision or put the party’s candidates in jeopardy while our applications are pending. We are asking the court to protect the subject of the appeal so that its eventual decision has practical effect,” Shaibu said.
The ADC said it is making its legal challenge public so Nigerians can understand precisely what is before the Court of Appeal. The party added that it will defend its rights, its leadership and the lawful decisions of its members through the courts.
“No one should use a contested judgment to alter the party’s records or disturb its candidates before the appellate court has had the opportunity to decide the issues placed before it,” it said.
